title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the first draft of the chapter 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic combinatorial-geometric framework. There is a set M of 'cells' (elements X, Y, ...). Each cell X has a closed cell-figure F_X. A family 𝓕 of 'figures' consists of finite sets of cells closed under faces. On it sit two relations. 'Subdivision/refinement' is written F' ≪ F, or s: F' ≅ F. 'Compatibility' means F ∪ G ∈ 𝓕. This is evidently a step toward the 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) announced in the Esquisse d'un programme.

On p.48 he defines F and G to be disjoint if they are compatible and F ∩ G = ∅. Cells X and Y are disjoint if F_X and F_Y are. He notes that disjointness passes to subfigures.

This page proves that disjointness and unions behave well under subdivision.

(Crossed-out first attempt, Cor 4/5.) If F and G are disjoint and F' subdivides F, then F' and G are disjoint. A crossed-out variant states the same with both sides subdivided.

C5. Let F' be a subdivision of F. For every figure G, F' and G are disjoint iff F and G are disjoint. NB: it suffices to prove this for elementary G (a single closed cell F_X). It then follows from C4 (p.47-48: subdivision versus compatible unions) that F' ∪ G is a subdivision of F ∪ G.

Cor. Let F and G be disjoint, and let F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G. Then F' and G' are disjoint and F' ∪ G' ≪ F ∪ G. If F' and G' are subdivisions of F and G, then F' ∪ G' is a subdivision of F ∪ G. Here subdivision means a refinement that is an 'isomorphism'. In modern terms, disjoint union is compatible with subdivision.

C6 (induced subdivisions). Let F be a figure, F' a subdivision of F, and G a subfigure of F. Then there is a unique subfigure G' ⊂ F' that is a subdivision of G. Explicitly, G' = {X ∈ F' | X ≪ G}. It is written F'|G. An NB notes the transitivity of induction: (F''|F')|G' = F''|G, i.e. restriction is functorial.

C7 (gluing of subdivisions) begins. Let F = ∪ F_i with F_i subfigures, and let F'_i be subdivisions of F_i. On the next page: if these agree on the overlaps F_i ∩ F_j, there is a unique subdivision F' of F with F'|F_i = F'_i.

In modern language, C6 and C7 together say that G ↦ {subdivisions of G} is a sheaf of sets on the finite 'space' of subfigures, for covers by subfigures. A corollary on p.50 gives the consequence: a subdivision is determined by its restrictions to the closed cells. This is the combinatorial backbone needed to treat tame spaces as glued from cells, with the subdivision category behaving like a site.
errors: No proofs are given on this page for C5 or C6; they are only stated with reductions. On p.50 Grothendieck himself observes that the fact that each X ∈ G' refines G does not by itself imply that G' refines G. So C6 needs an argument, supplied there via a common refining subdivision.
In the Cor after C5 the manuscript appears to read 'G' ≪ F'. It should be 'G' ≪ G'; this is a slip of the pen.
C5's 'iff' implicitly needs compatibility of G with F (resp. F') to transfer, which rests on C4. It is plausible within his axioms but not verified on the page.

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures is invariant under subdivision, and subdivision commutes with disjoint union
ideas.modern_name: Stability of disjoint union under subdivision in polyhedral/cell complexes

ideas.what: Induced subdivision F'|G on a subfigure; uniqueness; G' = {X ∈ F' : X ≪ G}; transitivity
Gluing of subdivisions compatible on overlaps (C7): subdivisions form a sheaf on subfigures
ideas.modern_name: Sheaf property of subdivisions; local-to-global for triangulations/cell decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in PL / o-minimal cell decomposition theory
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée); these axioms are unpublished

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'figures' and 'cells' framework for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology; compare o-minimal structures and regular CW/cell posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries, Knebusch, Shiota (o-minimal/semialgebraic); Grothendieck's own programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 announces the programme without this axiomatics

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops an explicit combinatorial axiomatics of 'figures' and 'subdivisions' as a foundation for tame topology. On this page it includes induced subdivisions and a sheaf-type gluing theorem. It was never published or developed by others in this form; the actual development of tame topology went through o-minimality instead.
missed.quote: C6 (Subdivisions induites) ... il existe une unique sous-figure G' de F', telle que G' soit subdivision de G ... C7 (Recollement des subdivisions)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The framework could be compared with current axiomatic or combinatorial approaches to tame and stratified spaces (exit-path categories, cell posets in o-minimal geometry). The individual lemmas on this page, however, are routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemmas are standard facts about subdivisions of cell complexes. Interest lies only in their being part of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame-topology draft, which carries a sheaf-like gluing viewpoint on subdivisions.
transcription_corrections: C5 reads roughly: 'Soient F une figure, F' une subdivision de F. Alors pour toute figure G, F' et G sont disjoints ssi F et G sont disjointes'. The transcription garbles this.
In the Cor after C5, the manuscript seems to write 'F'≪F, G'≪F' (a slip for G'≪G), then 'F' et G' sont disjointes, et F'∪G' ≪ F∪G'.
The marginal note reads 'NB Transitivité de l'induction (Double)' next to the line 'G'⊂F''.
The crossed-out top block is labelled 'Cor 4/5' and also contains a crossed 'Cor Si F' subdivise F, G' subdivise G, F et G disj. alors F' et G' disjointes'.
